decision: Keep CALABARZON visibly in progress. This checkpoint records the current source-backed leads and specific gaps; it is not a complete fish checklist, a completed region, or a public species release.

historicalSourcesWithSomeSpeciesLevelRes.note: Four historical locality assertions from four CC0 museum specimens; shared coordinate is withheld; the NFRDI reports are separate landed-catch or source leads.
One historical locality assertion derived from three CC0 museum records; date and coordinates are unknown.
One corrected 2024 preserved-specimen assertion; noncommercial CC BY-NC terms; no map point.
Twelve dated-paper table assertions in a separate reviewed projection; three source-family conflicts remain held; not a whole-river or current-presence list.
Four checklist assertions prepared from a source; three candidates held; no survey field date is adopted.

materialHeldOrUnavailable: Tayabas River: official abstract describes 15 aggregate species, but its table is unavailable and item-specific reuse rights are unresolved; three exact GBIF fish-locality strings returned zero.
Seven San Pablo lakes: one historical aggregate study lead; per-lake species rows held pending item-specific rights.
Manila Bay: historic trawl table and seven additional CAS named-bay candidates remain held; broad named-bay geometry is not a legal or Cavite boundary.
Brackish and estuarine leads: no admitted assertions tied to reviewed station salinity.
Several rivers, lakes, bays, wetlands, reservoirs and streams remain unreviewed or have only bounded locality-string checks.
Dagatan Lake: a DENR plan lists five local fish names, but no scientific identities, specimens or fish sampling date; item-level reuse terms and current protection status are unresolved.

The 11 new BMB/DENR CALABARZON water/habitat leads had 32 exact-name GBIF Actinopterygii searches across waterBody/locality fields (including five candidate spelling variants); all returned zero. This is a bounded discovery gap, not evidence of fish absence.

SEAFDEC 2016 Table 2 identifies a Bal-on Reservoir site and NIFEP group activities for several CALABARZON waters, but the San Pablo/Tadlak grouping is not allocated to individual lakes and six Rizal river sanctuaries are unnamed. The table gives no contemporary species survey.

SEAFDEC's 2016 proceedings reports a 7 ha Dagatan Lake in San Antonio at coordinates rounded to whole minutes and mentions Clarias macrocephalus without survey details; it does not resolve identity against Lake Pagatan or establish a dated occurrence.
evidenceReadout.zeroResultMeaning: Exact-locality zeroes are bounded search gaps, not fish-absence findings. Waterbird monitoring and historical common-name lists are not species-level fish presence evidence.

openGaps.reason: Eighty-three selected named water/habitat leads are seeded across CALABARZON water types. Historical BMB 2016/2019 and DENR 2024/2025 sources are partial and differently classified; none establishes today?s complete waterbody denominator. A visual review of selected Atlas pages added two river leads and one creek lead while retaining duplicate/compound rows as unresolved. Exact-name GBIF zeroes remain bounded discovery only; no absence or current fish status is inferred.
openGaps.nextAction: Continue source-derived locality and feature-identity review across all CALABARZON water types; resolve the DENR 2021 aggregate counts and obtain a named, auditable inventory before claiming complete regional coverage.

openGaps.reason: The official 2024 roadmap says 30 wetlands but lists 31 mixed name phrases. The 2019 BMB inventory adds historical named inland-wetland rows but is not directly comparable and does not resolve aliases, nested habitats or the count discrepancy.
openGaps.nextAction: Obtain the readable 2024 inventory and 2025 Table 8 through permitted official access; ask DENR how the 30 headline count maps to 31 phrases and whether there is a named inventory for the reported river systems. Do not equate name phrases to distinct wetlands or use them as a complete denominator.

openGaps.reason: Official indexed excerpts support starter identity leads, but direct requests returned 403 in this session. No local raw-source hash exists for these pages/PDFs.
openGaps.nextAction: Use a permitted browser/direct access route or alternative primary repository and create a receipt before detailed row extraction; no access-control bypass.

openGaps.reason: Two source-named estuary leads have no reviewed reach geometry or salinity profile. No fish evidence has been admitted for them.
openGaps.nextAction: Find study-specific station/reach/salinity evidence or retain unknown classifications.

openGaps.reason: Regional fish coverage remains incomplete across 83 selected research leads. Atlas inventories are not fish surveys. Bounded GBIF name-field zeroes identify discovery gaps; ambiguous candidates remain held and no absence or current fish status is inferred.
openGaps.nextAction: Join only independently reviewed evidence at its supported geographic scale.

openGaps.reason: No validated waterbody geometry or precise point assignment was created across 83 selected leads. Repeated names, source-era localities, compound river names and habitat-versus-waterbody identity remain under review.
openGaps.nextAction: Reconcile stable identities and source-era/current geography before map display.

openGaps.reason: Source registry entries are not bulk text/map/media reuse permissions or biological approval.
openGaps.nextAction: Complete dataset/record/field-level rights and citation review before generating public data.
